plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional plot of a single space curve rendered in dark blue against labeled coordinate axes. The vertical z-axis is graduated with ticks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. The x-axis runs toward the lower left with ticks labeled 2 and 4 in front and -2 and -4 behind, and the y-axis runs toward the lower right with the same labeling, 2 and 4 on the near side and -2 and -4 on the far side. The curve spirals counterclockwise around the vertical axis while climbing steadily, completing roughly two full turns between the xy-plane and the top of the frame above z = 12; its circular cross-section has radius 4, so each loop sweeps out past the ticks marked 4 on both horizontal axes. Two arrowheads placed on the ascending curve show the direction of travel. Across the upper right, in bold, the formula r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k is printed. Holding the loop radius constant while the height grows in step with the parameter is precisely what produces the spring-like shape. The plot displays the graph of a vector-valued function whose circular motion in the horizontal plane combines with uniform vertical rise to trace a helix.

elements: vertical z-axis with tick marks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12
x-axis running toward lower-left with ticks at 2, 4 (near) and -2, -4 (far)
y-axis running toward lower-right with ticks at 2, 4 (near) and -2, -4 (far)
dark blue helix of radius 4 rising from z=0 to above z=12 (t from 0 to 4π), about two full turns
two arrowheads on the curve indicating increasing-t direction of travel
moving point marker tracing the curve
faint radius line from the z-axis to the moving point
bold formula label r(t) = 4cos(t)i + 4sin(t)j + tk in the upper right
live readout of x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), z=t at the current parameter value

interactions.label: Trace r(t)
interactions.teaches: The helix is circular motion in the xy-plane combined with constant vertical rise — the moving point makes both components visible as the curve is drawn behind it

interactions.label: t
interactions.teaches: Each value of t maps to exactly one point (4cos t, 4sin t, t) — scrubbing t shows how the vector-valued function assigns position to time

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: From directly above the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle, revealing that the spiral is just constant-radius circular motion lifted by steadily increasing z

interactions.label: r(t) components
interactions.teaches: Editing the components reshapes the space curve — e.g. changing the radius, making z grow quadratically, or removing vertical rise entirely shows which term controls which feature of the helix

demo_steps.title: Follow the parameter
demo_steps.narration: Scrub t from 0 to 4π. The point sweeps around the z-axis while the live readout shows x and y oscillating and z climbing one-to-one with t.

demo_steps.title: Top view
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the top view: the helix projects onto a perfect circle of radius 4 — all the 'spring' shape comes from the z = t term.

demo_steps.title: Full trace
demo_steps.narration: Return to 3D and let the animation trace the whole curve, leaving the dark blue helix behind the moving point.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: helix radius 4 in the XY plane, height from z=0 to z=4π≈12.57 (about two turns, matching the source where the curve rises past the z=12 tick). Axes: z vertical spanning 0 to ~13 with labeled ticks every 2; x toward lower-left and y toward lower-right, each spanning ±5 with labeled ticks at ±2, ±4. Curve color dark blue #1a4f8a (matching source), radius ~0.03 tube. Two small cone arrowheads on the curve at roughly t≈3.5 and t≈7 pointing in the increasing-t direction. Moving point: orange #ff8800 sphere radius 0.15. Radius line from (0,0,z) to the point, thin grey dashed. Formula text upper right, bold black. Default camera azimuthDeg 35, elevationDeg 18 reproduces the source's slightly-above three-quarter look; Top view is elevation 90 straight down the z-axis.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the helix as a TubeGeometry along a CatmullRom curve sampled at ~400 points over t∈[0,4π]; rebuild it (and reposition arrowheads) whenever an equation field re-parses successfully — show parse errors inline and keep the last valid curve on failure. In Top view, keep the axes but drop the vertical perspective; animate the camera transition smoothly. Sync slider, animation, and equation input: animation drives paramT, and the point always sits at (x(t), y(t), z(t)) from the current parsed components.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for tracing r(t): the learner plays the motion, a point moves around the circle while rising at constant speed and leaves the helix behind, making the combination of circular horizontal motion and linear vertical motion visible.
- Slider for parameter t: the learner scrubs t, the point advances along the helix with live x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), and z=t values, showing how the vector-valued function maps time to position.
- Toggle between top view and 3D view: the learner switches views, the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle from above and returns to a rising spiral in 3D, clarifying that constant radius and increasing height together form the helix.
- Equation input for the parametric curve: learner edits x(t), y(t), and z(t), pre-filled with 4*cos(t), 4*sin(t), and t; the helix redraws and the moving point follows the new curve over the same t interval.

authoredContext:
As mentioned, the name of the shape of the curve of the graph in the examplec. is a helix (the figure). The curve resembles a spring, with a circular cross-section looking down along the z-axis. It is possible for a helix to be elliptical in cross-section as well. For example, the vector-valued function r(t)=4costi+3sintj+tk describes an elliptical helix. The projection of this helix into the x,y-plane is an ellipse. Last, the arrows in the graph of this helix indicate the orientation of the curve as t progresses from 0 to 4π.

The graph of the third vector-valued function is a helix.

This figure is the graph of a helix in the 3 dimensional coordinate system. The curve represents the function r(t) = cost i + sint j + tk. The curve spirals in a circular path around the vertical z-axis and has the look of a spring. The arrows on the curve represent orientation.
